title: Apple Signs Hiring and Licensing Deal With AI Podcast Startup Huxe
key_facts: A European Commission filing says Apple will have the right to make employment offers to certain Huxe employees.
Apple also receives a non-exclusive license to Huxe's intellectual property; it is not an outright acquisition.
Huxe was founded by former Google NotebookLM team members Raiza Martin, Jason Spielman and Stephen Hughes.
Huxe's app generated personalized audio briefings from users' emails, calendars and interests.
Huxe announced in May that it was winding down; its audio service ended on 28 May.
Apple notified the Commission of the arrangement on 9 June.
The filing does not say which employees Apple could recruit or whether anyone has been hired.
quote_evidence: The filing says Apple will have the right to make employment offers to certain Huxe employees and receive a non-exclusive license to the company's intellectual property, so this isn't an outright acquisition of the company.
The filing does not say which employees Apple could recruit, nor does it confirm whether anyone has actually been hired.
why_it_matters_hint: Apple gains AI audio know-how from a team whose own app has shut down, through a hiring-and-license deal rather than a purchase.
event_date: Apple notified the Commission on 9 June (year not stated, read as 2026); first reported 9 Oct 2026
notes: Filing itself not opened; MacRumors relays it. Treated as NEW because 9 Oct is the first public report.
